claims.text: The initial material is an additively manufactured dual-nanoprecipitation Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 HEA.
Atom probe tomography applied after high-temperature oxidation will reveal oxidation-induced elemental redistribution around nanoprecipitates.
Elemental redistribution around nanoprecipitates affects protective oxide formation.
The samples will be subjected to high-temperature oxidation and then characterized by APT.
Oxidation will be performed at controlled temperature and exposure time representative of high-temperature service.
Nanoprecipitates are expected to act as centers for elemental segregation.
Nanoprecipitate-associated elemental segregation influences oxide-layer formation and stability.
APT provides three-dimensional nanoscale compositional mapping.
APT can elucidate the redistribution of Ti and Cr during oxidation.
Redistribution of Ti and Cr mediates the development of oxidation barriers or degradation zones.
APT will detect localized elemental depletion or enrichment at or near nanoprecipitates in oxidized samples relative to unoxidized samples.
The detected elemental redistribution will correlate with improved or degraded oxidation resistance.
Cast or wrought counterparts have relatively uniform oxidation and elemental distributions that are less modified by additive manufacturing.
APT resolution and sample-preparation limitations may obscure subtle compositional gradients or complex multiphase interactions.
Large oxidation scales may cause APT results to vary or become difficult to obtain.
TEM-EDS can be used as a complementary method to validate segregation patterns observed by APT.
